explanation: transfer() acquires this's lock then other's lock. Two threads transferring in opposite directions can each hold one lock and block waiting for the other — a classic lock-ordering deadlock (thread A holds acctA, wants acctB; thread B holds acctB, wants acctA). The fix is to acquire locks in a consistent global order (e.g. by account id).
prompt: Two threads call transfer() in opposite directions at the same time. What's the bug?
choices: Two threads transferring opposite ways can each hold one lock and wait on the other — a lock-ordering deadlock
